transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (CTO), Priya (Head of ML), Marcus (Platform), Sofia (Security)

Summary: quick discovery to understand latency/throughput needs for real-time payments fraud detection use-case - p95 targets, streaming, concurrency and POC requirements.

[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you all hear me ok?
[00:05] Liam: yep loud and clear, thanks Jamie.
[00:12] Jamie: quick intros - I'm Jamie, AE for Redwood, ravi and maya are our SEs, we'll lean on them for the benchmark details.
[00:20] Priya: hi I'm Priya, we run the ML stack, mainly transformer models for fraud scoring; we also do streaming scoring on webhook events.
[00:28] Marcus: Marcus, platform infra - we manage k8s clusters, some on AWS and some on-prem for sensitive data.
[00:35] Sofia: Sofia - security/compliance, I'll be looking at encryption, audit logs, SOC2 stuff.
[00:40] Ravi: great, thanks. quick agenda - understand your p95 latency targets, concurrency, current token/sec, and discuss hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

[02:10] Priya: our main SLAs are p95 inference latency under 200ms for short sequences (<= 128 tokens) when streaming, and around 300ms for longer flows (>=512 tokens) is acceptable. We also need sub-250ms for customer-facing flows.
[02:40] Maya: ok so p95 200ms for short sequences, are these streaming token-by-token responses or batched full-response?
[02:48] Priya: streaming - we stream partial scores back as events arrive; it's important for realtime decisions.
[03:05] Ravi: got it. what concurrency are we talking about? peaks?
[03:12] Liam: peak concurrent inference around 80 simultaneous streams across a fleet; baseline concurrency ~20. Peak QPS translates roughly to 6-8k tokens/sec aggregate per region.
[03:30] Marcus: also want to avoid cross-regional fallbacks - data residency is important for EU customers.

[04:05] Jamie: quick clarifying question: are you using any KV cache or prefix caching today to reduce per-token compute?
[04:12] Priya: yes for some heuristics we cache last 50 tokens, but not for model KV cache - we haven't rolled that out yet.
[04:20] Ravi: that's helpful - Redwood has automatic prefix/KV caching we can enable; it helps p95 for repeated contexts.

[05:00] Priya: also curious about warm vs cold behavior - we see cold starts spike latency a lot in our current stack.
[05:12] Maya: on Dedicated we keep GPU pools warm and have burst capacity; hosted has warm pools but there can be cold starts on scale-up. we can run stress tests to quantify.
[05:30] Liam: can you quantify? like how much p95 penalty on cold starts?
[05:36] Ravi: depends on model and quantization; for an fp16 7B model on a warm instance p95 token latency can be <100ms for short tokens, cold starts can add a few hundred ms to the first request depending on loading and device warming.

[06:50] Marcus: our compliance team will want to see KMS integration and audit logs - and possibly a VPC/private control plane for production.
[06:58] Sofia: yep SOC2 is a requirement and we need to validate encryption-at-rest and in-transit, plus HSM/KMS support.
[07:20] Jamie: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) on Dedicated/Private and detailed audit logs in the console. We'll share the security whitepaper.

[08:10] Priya: back to throughput - token/sec benchmarks. what numbers do people typically see in hosted vs Dedicated?
[08:20] Ravi: rough numbers: for a single GPU with our optimized runtime - depending on model and quantization - you might see 2k-6k tokens/sec for autoregressive workloads on an A100-class instance; with quantized 4-bit kernels and batching you can push higher. Dedicated gives more predictable throughput; hosted can be fast but is subject to multi-tenant variance.
[08:55] Priya: so for our 6-8k tokens/sec aggregate per region we probably need 2-3 GPUs reserved?
[09:05] Maya: likely, yes - we can size a Dedicated pool; we'll run exact token/sec runs on your sample payloads.

[10:10] Liam: how does streaming latency tie to token/sec? if token/sec is high but per-token latency is elevated, that's a problem.
[10:18] Ravi: streaming p95 is influenced by model throughput per token and batching strategy - continuous batching can increase overall throughput but might add a few ms of batching delay. For strict p95 targets we configure smaller batch windows and enable KV caching.

[11:40] Priya: do you have examples of p95 numbers for streamed chat-typer workloads?
[11:48] Ravi: for a 7B model with continuous streaming and small batch windows our customers commonly see p95 token latency around 80-150ms in Dedicated; hosted numbers can be similar but with more variance. For 13B models expect higher.

[13:00] Marcus: what's the overhead for payload encryption and auth? we use mTLS and SAML SSO.
[13:08] Maya: Redwood supports mTLS and can integrate with SAML/SSO; encryption is handled at transport layer and you can use your KMS for key management; overhead is negligible compared to model runtimes.

[14:20] Priya: can we do a POC where you run our exact sample traces - varying sequence lengths (32, 128, 512) and streaming enabled, concurrency sweep 10/50/80?
[14:30] Jamie: yes that's the plan - Ravi will run the token/sec and p95 benchmarks and share a spreadsheet with results.

[15:09] (crosstalk)
[15:20] Ravi: for benchmarking I'll need sample payloads and a few representative prompts, plus your measured system load shape; that will let us simulate realistic batch and streaming behavior.
[15:35] Priya: we'll provide anonymized traces and a subset of prompts.

[16:10] Liam: what about fallback behavior - if Dedicated capacity is saturated can Redwood route to hosted or a lower-precision quantized variant?
[16:18] Maya: yes we have smart routing and automatic fallback policies - model variants and regions. You can configure fallbacks to cheaper quantized variants when capacity is hit.

[17:05] Sofia: auditability - are per-request logs available and how long do they retain them? we need 13 months retention for audit trails.
[17:15] Jamie: Redwood console supports configurable retention and you can export logs to your SIEM; for Private deployments you control retention fully. We'll include specifics in the security doc.

[18:40] Marcus: also interested in autoscaling - burst capacity behavior and warm pool sizes.
[18:50] Ravi: Dedicated supports configurable autoscale policies and a warm pool concept; you can pre-warm x instances for expected demand windows. For strict p95 SLAs we usually recommend a baseline warm pool sized to your 95th percentile traffic.

[20:10] Priya: what's the expected token/sec per GPU for quantized 4-bit on a T4-class vs A100-class?
[20:20] Ravi: ballpark: on A100 with optimized kernels you might see 4k-8k tokens/sec for a 7B quantized model; on T4s it's lower, maybe 1.5k-3k depending on sequence length and batch. We'll include specific benchmark numbers after we run your traces.

[22:00] Liam: any concerns about model compatibility - we use some custom RoBERTa-derived encoder-decoder flows and a custom head.
[22:10] Maya: runtime supports common transformer variants, and we can onboard custom model weights - SE team does compatibility checks as part of POC. There can be small changes for specific ops, we'll surface them.

[24:15] Priya: one more - streaming chunk size. if we stream every token it's higher overhead; can we configure to flush every N tokens?
[24:25] Ravi: yes you can configure flush intervals; many customers choose a 4-8 token flush for a balance between latency and overhead. We'll test with your service.

[26:00] Marcus: from infra side, for Private deployment what's the control plane model - fully customer-managed?
[26:08] Jamie: Private can be deployed in your VPC with a customer-managed control plane; on-prem is an option too. We'll share the deployment options doc.

[27:30] Sofia: legal - data residency in EU for EU customers, does Redwood guarantee no data egress?
[27:40] Jamie: with Private or Dedicated in-region we can provide isolation and data residency guarantees; we'll put the wording in the contract for legal review.

[29:05] Priya: ok so immediate deliverables are benchmark runs, security whitepaper, and Dedicated sizing/pricing.
[29:12] Jamie: correct - we'll aim to have initial benchmark spreadsheet by 2026-03-05 and pricing by 2026-03-04.

[30:00] (brief silence)
[30:15] Liam: how often does Redwood push runtime changes that could affect latency/regressions? we need stability.
[30:23] Maya: we version runtimes and support pinned model+runtime combos for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can opt into automatic updates or pin. We also provide regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.

[31:45] Priya: can we get an SLA for p95 latency on Dedicated?
[31:52] Jamie: SLA specifics depend on contract/commit level - for enterprise commitments we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include examples in the pricing doc.

[33:10] Marcus: one more question - can we run synthetic load tests from our infra into Redwood endpoints to validate latency from our network?
[33:18] Ravi: yes - we'll provide a benchmarking harness and guidance for client-side load generation. We can also run tests from Redwood to your endpoints if needed.

[34:40] Priya: that's great. any quick notes on cost tradeoffs - dedicated vs hosted for 24/7 low-latency needs?
[34:50] Jamie: Dedicated is usually more cost-effective at steady-state high-throughput and gives predictable p95s; hosted is better for variable workloads and fast time-to-value. We'll sketch three scenarios in the pricing doc.

[36:05] (wrap)
[36:12] Jamie: recap of next steps - Ravi runs benchmarks with your traces; Jamie shares pricing and Dedicated sizing; Sofia gets security docs; schedule technical deep dive next week.
[36:30] Liam: sounds good thanks everyone.
[36:35] Priya: thanks all.
[36:40] Sofia: thanks.
[36:45] (call ends)
